title: Degeneracy Counting Quantum Algorithm using Decoherence
authors: Malay Marut Das, Mark A. Novotny, Yaroslav Koshka
abstract: Counting the global optima of a classical optimization problem is a #P-hard task. We develop the canonical thermal pure quantum (CTPQ) state-based degeneracy counting (CTPQsd#) algorithm that determines the number of global optima of a classical optimization problem P by measuring only a small probe S, without finding individual minima. The method exploits a perturbative relation between the decoherence measure of S and the degeneracy of P when S and P are together in a CTPQ state. We provide the first numerical demonstration that this relation can be used to count the global minima, applying it to problems encoded by diagonal random-energy Hamiltonians as a maximally unstructured testbed for classical binary optimization problems. Classical simulations of up to 20 problem qubits quantify the algorithm's sensitivity to variations in the temperature of the CTPQ state, the Hamiltonian energy range, the problem size, and degeneracy. We establish the temperature threshold for determining the exact degeneracy and identify a second, lower threshold that provides a temperature window to count near-degenerate minima within a user-defined energy tolerance. By confining measurement to S, the protocol replaces tomography over the exponentially large problem Hilbert space with tomography over a small probe represented by only four qubits.
summary: The paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm to count the number of global minima in hard optimization problems without needing to find any individual minimum. It achieves this by measuring only a small probe system's decoherence, leveraging a theoretical link between this measure and the problem's degeneracy. The results demonstrate its feasibility on random-energy Hamiltonians, offering a scalable approach for quantum computation.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the degeneracy (number of global optima) of a classical optimization problem, which is known to be \#P-hard.
main_result: A novel algorithm ($	ext{CTPQ}_{	ext{sd}\#}$) was developed that estimates this degeneracy by measuring only a small probe system ($S$), circumventing the need for full Hilbert space tomography.
method: The method exploits a perturbative relationship between the decoherence measure of the small probe $S$ and the ground-state degeneracy of the large problem Hamiltonian $H_P$, when the combined system is prepared in a Canonical Thermal Pure Quantum (CTPQ) state.
model_or_system: The algorithm applies to classical optimization problems encoded by diagonal random-energy Hamiltonians, modeled as an interaction between a small probe ($S$) and the large problem environment ($P$).
key_observables: Decoherence measure ($\sigma_S$), thermalization measure ($\delta_S$), and the estimated ground-state degeneracy ($g_{P,	ext{Meas}}$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), energy range ($R$), problem size ($N_P$), and a user-defined energy tolerance ($\Delta g_P$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the existence of a perturbative relation in the low-temperature limit, and simulations are restricted to classical (diagonal) Hamiltonians.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of the absolute error for approximate degeneracy counting, revealing a two-threshold regime ($T_2 < T < T_1$), alongside plots showing decoherence ($\sigma_S$) vs. temperature.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the $	ext{CTPQ}_{	ext{sd}\#}$ algorithm based on theoretical relations derived from open quantum systems, demonstrates its application to diagonal random-energy Hamiltonians via numerical simulation, and systematically analyzes parameter dependence (temperature, energy range) to establish operational thresholds for counting.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, resource-efficient quantum protocol that bypasses the exponential scaling of full system tomography by encoding complex combinatorial counts into measurable decoherence properties of a small ancillary system.
